title: Swimming Champion Archie Goodburn to Deliver Rugby Match Ball in Front of 60,000 Fans
summary:
Champion swimmer Archie Goodburn is swapping the pool for a rugby stadium — just for one very special moment. On Sunday, November 15, the 25-year-old from Edinburgh will deliver the match ball for Scotland's Nations Championship game against Australia at Murrayfield, in front of more than 60,000 fans.

Goodburn is a British champion and a European bronze medallist, and he holds the Scottish record for the 50-metre breaststroke. But lately he has been racing for something bigger than medals. In 2024 he was diagnosed with a rare brain tumour called an oligodendroglioma. After surgery, he fought his way back to competitive swimming — and began campaigning for better brain cancer treatment and research.

His campaign has carried him a long way. In recent weeks, he has taken it to Prime Minister Andy Burnham and to Scotland's First Minister, John Swinney. The campaign aims to bolster treatment and research for brain cancer.

Being guest of honour at Murrayfield is a homecoming, too. Goodburn once played rugby himself, at blindside flanker for Stewart's-Melville College, before concentrating on swimming. Big crowds do not scare him either: at age 12 he sang a solo, 'What a Wonderful World,' in front of 10,000 people on the castle esplanade for the Edinburgh Military Tattoo.

'This means the absolute world to me,' he said.

Fans at the match will also be able to donate to two charities helping people with brain cancer: Brain Tumour Research and the Astro Brain Tumour Fund.

'Things are beginning to move,' Goodburn said, 'and this kind of initiative can make a difference.'
why_it_matters: Goodburn's appearance links a huge sporting crowd to brain cancer research, a cause that affects patients and families, including young people. It also shows how an athlete can use sporting fame to push for better treatment for others.

background_read: Delivering the match ball is an honour at big rugby games: a special guest carries the ball onto the pitch before kick-off, in front of the whole crowd.
Murrayfield, in Edinburgh, is the home stadium of Scotland's national rugby team.

A brain tumour is a growth of cells inside the brain. Some kinds can be removed with surgery, but treatment is difficult, which is why people who have had the illness often campaign for better treatment and more research.
Goodburn's story mixes both of his sports: he played rugby at school before concentrating on swimming, so appearing at Murrayfield brings the two together.
